findings.decompiled: while idx < targets.length: require cd[32 * idx + targets + 36] == address(cd[32 * idx + targets + 36]) / if address(cd[32 * idx + targets + 36]) == this.address: revert with 'Timelock/self-calls-disabled'
findings.source: Timelock.sol:97-99 for (uint256 i = 0; i < targets.length; ++i) { require(targets[i] != address(this), 'Timelock/self-calls-disabled'); }
findings.issue: Elements of the calldata array parameter targets are printed as raw offset arithmetic, although the text names the parameter and its length (targets.length).
findings.rule: cd[p + 36 + 32*i] for a calldata array parameter p of static elements is p[i] (and address(p[i]) after its range check).

notes: Source loops (3, all whiles): Timelock.scheduleBatch's self-call check (854), TimelockController.scheduleBatch's CallScheduled loop (919/949 area), TimelockController.executeBatch's execute loop (672). Implicit whiles: validated ABI decodings and re-encodings of address[]/uint256[]/bytes[] for hashOperationBatch (362, 378 and copies), and this version's storage of the whole batch: copies of targets/values/payloads into the operation record (1058, 1097), clearing of old storage arrays in cancel/execute/schedule (446, 821, 1142, loops over the bytes[] slots with short/long encoding tests), and a rotated storage-to-memory copy in the batch getter (478, P3). All functions were reviewed by reading (the largest is scheduleBatch, 323 lines); faithful. Role checks print as hasRole[role][caller] with the role hash constant.
summary: Faithful, readable text with all three source loops found; remaining whiles are ABI and storage copies of the batch arrays, and calldata array elements stay raw offsets.
